verdict.rationale: Grafana documents its own provisioning and observability-as-code features, which let you define dashboards, data sources, and other configurations in files you can keep in version control and deploy through CI/CD. Review and rollback are never documented, though, and would only come from external Git workflows, and alert-rule automations are not explicitly named as as-code resources. Missing for 10: first-party review/approval of automation changes, documented rollback or version history for alerts and automations, explicit coverage of alert rules as code, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: You can define data sources and dashboards using files that can be version controlled, making GitOps more natural.
This approach lets you define dashboards, data sources, and other configurations in code, enabling version control, automated testing, and reliable deployments through CI/CD pipelines.
It’s suitable for CI/CD pipelines, local development
